name: Canals (Undercity)
summary: In the Undercity, green slime fills the Canals between its quarters. The murky channels carry waste and mark the Forsaken's underground stronghold.

sections.title: A Toxic Moat
sections.body: Beneath Lordaeron's ruins, green sludge fills the Canals. The stone channels circle the Undercity and divide its quarters. They carry industrial refuse, chemical runoff, and alchemical waste instead of flowing water. Faint light shines through the liquid, and foul vapors rise from it. Water Walking cannot carry anyone across. Still, desperate anglers sometimes pull strange, tainted curiosities from the muck.

faq.q: What is the green liquid in the canals?
aliases: what is the slime in undercity
faq.answer: The green liquid is alchemical sludge made from toxic runoff, plague byproducts, and industrial waste gathered in the Undercity's drains. It is tainted and noxious, unlike clean water.

faq.q: Can you fish in the Undercity canals?
faq.answer: Yes. Patient anglers can cast into the sludge and sometimes pull up sickly, contaminated fish or discarded junk. Among it are old human skulls from Lordaeron's fallen past.

faq.q: Why doesn't Water Walking work on the canals?
aliases: why cant i walk on water undercity
faq.answer: The thick chemical slurry does not behave like natural water. Its foul, viscous makeup keeps shamans and other spellcasters from using ordinary Water Walking magic on it.

angles.text: For the Forsaken, the foul canals do no harm to their unliving bodies. They carry chemical runoff through the underground realm and serve as a moat.
As a shaman, you find the elements have little sway over the polluted muck in the Undercity's waterways. Ordinary spells like Water Walking fail there.
